how_selected: scripts/fill_author.py reads decisions.C1 and decisions.C2 of the core analysis output (labels, reasons, three-statistic label, interpretation flags) and picks one variant per slot; placeholders <<name>> are filled from the same output through the field paths of fill_core.py. DISC.interpretation = C1 part + C1 qualifiers (margin-limited, decay, reversed, exploratory) + C2 part. fill_author.py computes no number: DISC.code and CONCL.code carry no number and follow the registered C1 label alone (confirmed, confirmed in the pooled test only, refuted, inconclusive); without decisions.C1 they stay pending.

C1.C1-A: In the exploratory 20-draw control, norm-matched random directions in the same experts followed the routing contrast with an elasticity close to 1 (1.04 [0.99, 1.09]), the value the account gives for perturbations without alignment (statement C1-R), and produced 78\% of the symmetrized crossover. Routing mass therefore gates how strongly an old corpus is exposed to any change of the adapted experts, whatever the update learns, as expected if the routing weights scale the effect of any displacement of an expert. The learned updates exceeded them in each draw, by 0.30 on average (<<smr>> <<smr_ci>> on the six registered control draws); we read this excess as the alignment term, an alignment of the learned updates with the directions to which the old corpora are sensitive, which the account of Section~\ref{sec:account} does not derive and which remains a conjecture. The evidence comes from two MoE bases of the size and token budget used here, adapted on books only, so it does not extend to larger models, longer pretraining or other targets. It agrees with reports that forgetting concentrates in the parameters that the old data use, for routes in MoE models \citep{chen2026multihead} and for the output embeddings of tokens absent from the new corpus in dense models \citep{han2026deafening}, although neither study tests a registered crossover.
C1.C1-B: The crossover of learned updates did not exceed that of norm-matched random directions in the same experts (symmetrized minus random-direction crossover <<smr>> <<smr_ci>>), so the localization of forgetting by routing mass belongs to where an update of fixed size lands, as the accounting identity predicts for any such update (Section~\ref{sec:predictions}), and is not shown to be specific to learning. Its practical content is a forecast: before any adaptation run, the routing masses at the pretrained weights indicate on which old corpora forgetting will land, and the scoring of the pre-adaptation forecasters (Section~\ref{sec:secondary}), reported separately, tests how well probes at $\theta_0$ make this forecast. The evidence comes from two MoE bases of the size and token budget used here, adapted on books only, so it does not extend to larger models, longer pretraining or other targets.
C1.C1-D: The crossover was significant in the pooled test, but mean $J$ was not positive in <<nonpos_bases>>, so it did not replicate across the two bases. Since the bases differ only in their seed, this leaves open whether the localization is a property of routed models or of one training run; the replication on a third base (Section~\ref{sec:secondary}), reported separately, bears on this question. The evidence comes from two MoE bases of the size and token budget used here, adapted on books only, so it does not extend to larger models, longer pretraining or other targets.
C1.C1-F: Norm-matched random directions followed the routing masses while learned updates did not (upper 95\% bounds of $\bhat$, $\bpin$ and $\bsym$ below <<beta_ref>>; $\bhat=<<b>>$ <<b_ci>>, $\brand=<<brand>>$ <<brand_ci>>), so routing mass localizes the forgetting of fixed-size perturbations, and the learned updates of books adaptation do not follow it. By the three statistics (Table~\ref{tab:threestat}), what fails are the assumptions that random directions do not need, incoherent update directions (B3) and the leading-order expansion (B4), while the pinned and symmetrized statistics rule out re-routing and first-order transfer as the reason. For methods that choose the experts to adapt from routing statistics, this means that routing masses at the pretrained weights do not by themselves predict the forgetting of learned updates in these bases; it does not show that such methods fail by their own criteria.
C1.C1-G: Neither learned updates nor norm-matched random directions followed the routing masses (upper 95\% bounds of $\bhat$, $\bpin$, $\bsym$ and $\brand$ below <<beta_ref>>; $\bhat=<<b>>$ <<b_ci>>), so in these bases routing mass does not localize forgetting. By the three statistics (Table~\ref{tab:threestat}), what fails is an assumption that random directions also need, such as separable sensitivity (B5) or its homogeneity within the subsets (B6). For methods that choose the experts to adapt from routing statistics, this means that routing masses at the pretrained weights do not predict where forgetting lands in these bases; it does not show that such methods fail by their own criteria.
C1.C1-R: Learned updates did not follow the routing masses (upper 95\% bounds of $\bhat$, $\bpin$ and $\bsym$ below <<beta_ref>>; $\bhat=<<b>>$ <<b_ci>>), and the random-direction statistic $\brand=<<brand>>$ <<brand_ci>> did not settle whether routing mass localizes fixed-size perturbations, so the refutation concerns learned updates and leaves the localization itself open. For methods that choose the experts to adapt from routing statistics, this means that routing masses at the pretrained weights do not by themselves predict the forgetting of learned updates in these bases; it does not show that such methods fail by their own criteria.
C1.C1-I: The raw statistic fell below the margin while the symmetrized statistic, which cancels first-order terms, did not ($\bsym=<<bsym>>$ <<bsym_ci>>), so by the registered rule the raw crossover was distorted by first-order transfer and C1 is not refuted. A decisive test in this regime would need a target with little first-order transfer to code and mathematics, or a design that registers the symmetrized statistic as the primary one.
C1.C1-J: The crossover was positive but not significant (mean $J=<<mj>>$, Holm-adjusted $p=<<p_holm>>$), as the underpowered flag of gate G2-1 had warned before the freeze. A decisive study would need more draws per base or more bases than registered here; the power analysis of Appendix~\ref{app:power} and the noise estimate of gate G2-1 set the scale of that increase.
C1.C1-K.E1: C1 is inconclusive because <<e1_div>> of its <<e1_runs>> runs diverged, more than the registered share allows, so the registered test was not decided and the localization of forgetting by routing mass remains untested here. A decisive study would need an adaptation recipe that keeps the runs stable, with the number of draws of the power analysis (Appendix~\ref{app:power}).
C1.C1-K.none: C1 is inconclusive because no draw was usable, so the registered test was not decided and the localization of forgetting by routing mass remains untested here.
C1.C1-K.ml: The upper bounds of $\bhat$, $\bpin$ and $\bsym$ lay below <<beta_ref>>, but <<ml_bases>> <<ml_verb>> margin-limited at gate G0-7, and the registered rule allows no refutation then, so C1 is inconclusive. A decisive study would need bases whose sensitivity imbalance at the pretrained weights stays below the cap of the margin.
C1.C1-K.ub: The crossover was not significant (mean $J=<<mj>>$, Holm-adjusted $p=<<p_holm>>$), and its upper bounds did not fall below <<beta_ref>> ($\bhat=<<b>>$ <<b_ci>>), so the registered rule gives neither a confirmation nor a refutation. A decisive study would need more draws per base or more bases than registered here; the power analysis of Appendix~\ref{app:power} and the noise estimate of gate G2-1 set the scale of that increase.

C1_qualifiers.C1-C: In <<ml_bases>> the margin was capped at gate G0-7, before any adaptation run, so a pool effect of the size of the measured sensitivity imbalance is not excluded there.
C1_qualifiers.C1-E: The registered rule qualifies the C1 result as substantially decay-driven; decay alone changed the loss of the old corpora by at most 0.0006 nats, and Section~\ref{sec:limitations} explains why the rule fired.
C1_qualifiers.C1-H: The crossover had the opposite sign to the prediction; the account derives no mechanism for a reversal, and we do not propose one.
C1_qualifiers.C1-X: C1 entered the analysis as exploratory, as recorded at the freeze, so this reading carries no registered decision.

C2.C2-A: C2 is the forgetting side of known optimizer properties: under SGD an expert's displacement grows with its target routing mass, whereas Muon-type updates are steepest descent under a spectral norm and give same-shape experts updates of similar size \citep{bernstein2024old,vaidya2026expertmuoncompass}, and at step <<s>> forgetting followed target routing mass more strongly under SGD ($\Delta e=<<de>>$; five draws give no finite interval). The result concerns SGD at the calibrated learning rate $c/3$ and the earliest step that resolved forgetting. At that rate three of the eight SGD runs on high-usage subsets diverged, and the other five had a target loss above its starting value at step <<s>>, so the contrast reflects the instability of SGD on experts that the target uses heavily and does not isolate a forgetting mechanism. Later steps, other learning rates and a comparison at equal target gain lie outside the registered design. The Muon arm was not free of the dependence either: its elasticity estimate at step <<s>> was 0.341, and the step-8 equivalence analysis did not place it within the margin of one third (90\% interval [0.256, 0.419]).
C2.C2-B: At step <<s>> DCLM forgetting depended on target routing mass alike under both optimizers (upper 95\% bound of $\Delta e$ <<de_ub>>, below <<beta_ref>>), contrary to the derived prediction. The account offers candidate reasons without a new mechanism: a sensitivity term tied to the identity of the updated experts rather than to their routing mass, the five-step Newton--Schulz iteration of Muon in bf16 (NS-5), whose exactness is covered by a unit test only, gradient noise, through which routing enters Muon updates (gate G2-5 reports the per-expert gradient signal-to-noise ratio), and a first-order regime at small steps.
C2.C2-C: At step <<s>> the optimizer contrast was not resolved (mean $J2=<<mj2>>$, Holm-adjusted $p=<<p2_holm>>$; $\Delta e=<<de>>$ <<de_ci>>). The candidate reasons for a weak contrast, a sensitivity term tied to the identity of the updated experts rather than to their routing mass, the five-step Newton--Schulz iteration of Muon in bf16 (NS-5), whose exactness is covered by a unit test only, gradient noise, through which routing enters Muon updates (gate G2-5 reports the per-expert gradient signal-to-noise ratio), and a first-order regime at small steps, remain open, and a decisive test would need more than the <<D2>> registered draws.
C2.C2-C.none: C2 is inconclusive because no draw was usable, so the optimizer prediction remains untested here.
C2.C2-C.E1: C2 is inconclusive because more than the registered share of its runs diverged, so the optimizer prediction remains untested here.
C2.C2-D: The SGD arm did not realize the predicted displacement contrast (mean $D_{\mathrm{SGD}}/\Delta_Q=<<manip>>$), so by the registered rule C2 is uninformative and the optimizer prediction remains untested; a decisive test would need a learning rate and step at which SGD displacements follow target routing mass.
C2.C2-E: C2 was exploratory under the registered gates; at step <<s>> forgetting followed target routing mass more strongly under SGD ($\Delta e=<<de>>$ <<de_ci>>), in line with the known optimizer properties \citep{bernstein2024old,vaidya2026expertmuoncompass}, but without a registered decision.
C2.C2-F: C2 was exploratory under the registered gates, and its estimate at step <<s>> ($\Delta e=<<de>>$ <<de_ci>>) carries no registered decision.
C2.C2-F0: C2 was exploratory under the registered gates and carries no registered decision.

Most of this difference does not depend on what the update learns, since norm-matched random directions in the same experts produced about four fifths of the symmetrized crossover in the registered six-draw control and 78\% in an exploratory 20-draw extension; routing mass gates how much of any change to the adapted experts reaches an old corpus. Whether the routing masses at $\theta_0$ rank arbitrary update sets, and whether they do so for targets other than books, was not tested.

variants.C2-A: At step <<s>>, the earliest step that resolved forgetting, this was the case on the five draws that remained after three SGD divergences ($\Delta e=<<de>>$; five draws give no finite interval). The SGD runs on high-usage subsets forgot 0.039 to 0.438 nats of DCLM, 46 to 828 times as much as the SGD runs on low-usage subsets (0.0005 to 0.0011 nats), before they had learned the target, while under Muon both kinds of subset stayed below 0.001 nats. SGD at this learning rate was thus unstable on the experts that the target uses most; the result compares that phase with stable Muon and does not isolate a forgetting mechanism, and the Muon runs stop at step <<s>>, so later steps are not covered.
variants.C2-B: At step <<s>> DCLM forgetting depended on target routing mass alike under both optimizers (upper 95\% bound of $\Delta e$ <<de_ub>>), so at that step the update set carried the same share of the protection under SGD and Muon.
variants.C2-C: At step <<s>> the optimizer contrast was not resolved ($\Delta e=<<de>>$ <<de_ci>>), so whether the optimizer shifts the protection to the update set remains open.
variants.C2-C0: C2 was inconclusive, so whether the optimizer shifts the protection to the update set remains open.
variants.C2-D: The SGD arm missed its registered displacement contrast, so C2 says nothing about the optimizer as a lever.
variants.C2-E: C2 was exploratory; its estimate at step <<s>> ($\Delta e=<<de>>$ <<de_ci>>) points the way of the prediction but carries no registered decision about the optimizer as a lever.
variants.C2-F: C2 was exploratory, and its estimate at step <<s>> ($\Delta e=<<de>>$ <<de_ci>>) carries no registered decision about the optimizer as a lever.
variants.C2-F0: C2 was exploratory and carries no registered decision about the optimizer as a lever.

variants.CODE.conf: In the C1 test the forgetting of code and mathematics followed the routing masses of the adapted experts (Section~\ref{sec:res-c1}); among the feed-forward experts of these MoE models this is the property that a choice of modules by routing statistics requires, and whether it carries over to adapters selected once per task is not tested here.<<x_code>><<code2>>
variants.CODE.pooled: In the C1 test the forgetting of code and mathematics followed the routing masses of the adapted experts in the pooled test of the two MoE bases, but not in each base (Section~\ref{sec:res-c1}); the property that a choice of modules by routing statistics requires is therefore not established for each model, and whether it would carry over to adapters selected once per task is not tested here.<<x_code>><<code2>>
variants.CODE.ref: In the C1 test the forgetting of code and mathematics did not follow the routing masses of the adapted experts (Section~\ref{sec:res-c1}), so these runs give no support for choosing the modules to update by routing statistics in order to protect code.<<x_code>><<code2>>
variants.CODE.inc: The C1 test was inconclusive (Section~\ref{sec:res-c1}), so these runs leave open whether the forgetting of code follows the routing masses of the adapted experts, the property that a choice of modules by routing statistics requires.<<x_code>><<code2>>

DISC.code.second_stream: Section~\ref{sec:res-est} also reports the crossover on the second code stream.
DISC.code.exploratory_suffix: C1 entered the analysis as exploratory, so this reading carries no registered decision.

variants.CODE.conf: In these runs the forgetting of code and mathematics in the two MoE bases followed the routing masses of the adapted feed-forward experts, as such a choice requires; the registered code stream is mathematics-related code, and on general Python code, the secondary stream, the elasticity was 1.820 [1.727, 1.914] (unadjusted). Whether this carries over to adapters selected once per task is open.
variants.CODE.pooled: In these runs the forgetting of code and mathematics followed the routing masses of the adapted feed-forward experts only in the pooled test of the two MoE bases, not in each base.
variants.CODE.ref: In these runs the forgetting of code and mathematics did not follow the routing masses of the adapted feed-forward experts, so they give no support for such a choice.
variants.CODE.inc: In these runs the question remained open.
